title: Learn the Network at your pace.
intro: Return any time for a short path through the live RFxchange workflows available to your organization. Your guide progress never grants permission or changes a business record.
recommendationBoundary: A recommendation uses current organization context only. It does not grant organization permission, issuer authority, Official Resource Provider status, verification, credibility, or commercial access.
catalogUpdate: This guide has new reviewed content. Your earlier progress remains visible; review the current version when ready.
pathNavigation: Quick Start and role learning paths
explainerDismissed: Explanation closed. You can reopen it here at any time.

questions.happens: What happens if I do this?

states.saved: Education progress saved for this user and organization.
states.error: Education progress could not be saved. Reload and try again.

quickStart.title: Quick Start
quickStart.summary: Follow the Network value spine using only live, authorized Wave 3 workflows.

understand.title: Make your organization understandable
understand.body: Review the organization profile, confirmed capabilities, evidence, visibility, and operating context.

discover.title: See how organizations become discoverable
discover.body: Use the controlled locality map and Network search without changing geographic authority.

connect.title: Make a consented connection
connect.body: Learn referral purpose, exact recipient, shared fields, and lifecycle before sending.

act.title: Act through current resources
act.body: Find maintained provider services, make an exact request, and use published resources.

business.title: Business path
business.summary: Build a clear organization presence, discover capability, connect with consent, and use current support resources.

profile.title: Confirm your market profile
profile.body: Suggestions remain non-authoritative until an authorized person confirms a separate organization claim.

discovery.title: Explore the controlled Network
discovery.body: Search published organization projections within server-authorized geography.

referrals.title: Send or respond to referrals
referrals.body: Share only the displayed context and preserve acceptance, decline, contact, and close as separate facts.

resources.title: Find provider support
resources.body: Compare explicit service territory, maintained availability, and explainable routing reasons.

rfx.title: Create or respond to an RFx
rfx.body: RFx creation and participant response are planned for Wave 4 and are not available in this guide.

credibility.title: Use credibility evidence
credibility.body: Credibility scoring and seals are planned separately. Profile evidence does not create credibility.

issuer.title: Issuer path
issuer.summary: Learn the future Need → Capability relationship while using only current Network research and resources.

market.title: Research the current market
market.body: Explore confirmed organization capabilities and controlled locality context before a future need is authored.

resources.title: Understand support resources
resources.body: See current provider services and published resources without treating them as issuer qualification.

rfx.title: Author and publish an RFx
rfx.body: Issuer authoring, requirements, release, and evaluation are planned for Wave 4 and remain unavailable.

evaluation.title: Evaluate responses and outcomes
evaluation.body: Evaluator authority, awards, outcomes, and analytics are not implemented and are not simulated here.

resourceProvider.title: Resource Provider path
resourceProvider.summary: Understand the controlled application, official status, service publication, requests, communications, and resources.

application.title: Apply through the governed workflow
application.body: An application references current organization identity and evidence; it does not self-approve the organization.

profile.title: Maintain the private service profile
profile.body: Approved managers maintain categories, services, eligibility, intake, territory, and availability.

discovery.title: Publish for provider discovery
discovery.body: Only explicit publication makes selected services discoverable; official status alone does not.

requests.title: Respond to exact provider requests
requests.body: Accept, decline, redirect, and message within the request while keeping connection separate from service outcome.

publication.title: Publish governed resources
publication.body: Draft, publish, withdraw, and expiry are explicit states with participant-authored content preserved.

credentials.title: Earn training or certification
credentials.body: Paid training, certification, credibility, and commercial entitlement are planned separately and unavailable.

profile-confirmation.title: Confirm organization profile information
profile-confirmation.what: This writes an organization-owned profile or market-context fact through the authorized workflow.
profile-confirmation.why: Discovery and routing should use reviewed organization facts, not draft interface text.
profile-confirmation.happens: The server rechecks your current organization and permission, validates the value, and records versioned evidence.
profile-confirmation.next: The confirmed fact may appear only in projections allowed by its visibility; it does not create verification or credibility.

capability-suggestion.title: Review a capability suggestion
capability-suggestion.what: This is an AMACS 0.5.0-grounded suggestion, not an organization claim.
capability-suggestion.why: The organization must decide whether the concept accurately describes what it does.
capability-suggestion.happens: Accept, edit, reject, or leave unresolved. Disposition remains separate from the later authoritative write.
capability-suggestion.next: Only a separate current-authority command can create or update a confirmed capability claim.

credential-evidence.title: Add credential or evidence information
credential-evidence.what: This records organization-provided credential or evidence metadata with provenance.
credential-evidence.why: Evidence can support understanding, but it is not automatically proof of a capability or independent verification.
credential-evidence.happens: The record is saved within the organization boundary and published only under its explicit visibility state.
credential-evidence.next: Any later evidence relationship, verification, or credibility decision remains separate and governed.

media-visibility.title: Choose media visibility
media-visibility.what: This controls whether an organization-owned media item stays private or appears in an allowed projection.
media-visibility.why: Uploaded material can contain sensitive or participant-authored information.
media-visibility.happens: The chosen visibility and provenance are persisted; private storage remains server-authorized.
media-visibility.next: Publication can be changed through its own workflow and does not translate or endorse the authored content.

additional-location.title: Confirm an additional location
additional-location.what: This adds a subordinate organization location with explicit privacy and geography handling.
additional-location.why: A location affects map presentation, while geography participation remains controlled server-side.
additional-location.happens: The server validates the selected candidate and stores exact, approximate, or locality-only presentation rules.
additional-location.next: A subordinate marker may appear only when its authoritative and privacy conditions are satisfied.

referral-consent.title: Send a consented referral
referral-consent.what: This creates an organization-owned introduction for the exact recipient and displayed shared fields.
referral-consent.why: A referral shares business context and must not disclose more than the sender reviewed.
referral-consent.happens: The acknowledgement, referral, lifecycle event, and any notification intent are persisted separately.
referral-consent.next: The recipient may accept or decline. Sending does not prove contact, service, qualification, or outcome.

referral-response.title: Respond to a referral
referral-response.what: This records the recipient organization’s explicit accept or decline decision.
referral-response.why: A response changes referral lifecycle, not the truth of a business outcome.
referral-response.happens: The server checks recipient authority and expected version before appending the transition evidence.
referral-response.next: Accepted, contacted, and closed remain separate later states; decline creates no negative credibility signal.

provider-application.title: Submit Resource Provider information
provider-application.what: This governed application references your current organization, authority, location, service geography, and evidence.
provider-application.why: Official Resource Provider status is an administrative decision separate from organization authority and Verification.
provider-application.happens: A draft may be submitted for scoped review; saving or submitting never self-approves the organization.
provider-application.next: An authorized reviewer may request information, approve, or deny with preserved decision evidence.

provider-connection.title: Connect with this provider
provider-connection.what: This sends a request to the exact published provider service you selected.
provider-connection.why: Territory and availability help explain fit but do not promise capacity, eligibility, or service.
provider-connection.happens: The displayed organization and summary are shared after consent through the referral lifecycle.
provider-connection.next: The provider may accept, decline, redirect, or message. Connection is not a service outcome.

provider-response.title: Respond to a provider request
provider-response.what: This records the Official Resource Provider organization’s response to one exact request.
provider-response.why: A response must preserve who was asked and must not imply a broader availability or qualification decision.
provider-response.happens: Accept, decline, or redirect appends a versioned request transition after current authority is checked.
provider-response.next: Request-scoped messages may continue; service delivery, payment, verification, and outcome remain outside this state.

provider-resource-publication.title: Publish a provider resource
provider-resource-publication.what: This moves provider-authored resource content from draft to an explicit Network or public publication state.
provider-resource-publication.why: Participants need to distinguish maintained provider content from RFxchange endorsement or qualification.
provider-resource-publication.happens: The server checks provider authority, expected version, visibility, timing, and publication lifecycle.
provider-resource-publication.next: The resource can be withdrawn or expire. Publication creates no ranking, credibility seal, or guaranteed result.
